issues.description: default_raise() and the kw_only_dataclass comment retain dead 3.9-compatibility scaffolding that is now provably unreachable.
issues.detail: The PR removes the version branch but leaves `def default_raise()` with the comment 'for < 3.10 compatibility' and a similar comment block above TransactionEndpointRequest. If the compatibility shim is gone, the helper that existed only because `field(default_factory=default_raise)` was needed under 3.9 must be re-justified or removed. Keep code only when its precondition still holds; otherwise it is folklore.

issues.description: Three Ruff rules (UP007, UP035, UP045) are silenced with a TODO instead of executed as part of the stated specification.
issues.detail: The PR description claims `Union`/`Optional` will be banned, yet the enforcement is disabled wholesale with 'it's a lot of errors'. This is precisely the substitution of intention for proof. Either the postcondition (no Union/Optional) holds and the rules stay enabled, or it does not and the description is misleading. Pick one; do not ship both.

issues.description: Install.sh and Install.ps1 still accept Python 3.10 while pyproject requires >=3.10, but the shell guard permits 3.7-3.12.
issues.detail: install.sh line 138 still tests `PYTHON_MINOR_VER < 7`, which would accept 3.7-3.9 silently if the search loop ever matched them. The loop was tightened but the postcondition check was not. The two predicates must agree: minimum supported version is a single fact, not two. Tighten the guard to `< 10` or prove the loop makes that branch unreachable.

issues.description: test-install-scripts.yml runs `dnf search python3.12` as a side effect with no assertion on its output.
issues.detail: A `search` command in a CI prep step either gates installation or it is noise. Here it does neither: failure is ignored, success is unused. This is defensive-as-substitute for actually verifying the package is available before `dnf install`. Remove it or use it as a precondition check with a fail-fast assertion.

issues.description: conditions.py still carries the 'continue # pragma: no cover' branch whose comment was the only thing justifying it.
issues.detail: The removed comment explained why coverage tooling missed the branch on 3.9. With 3.9 gone, either the branch is now covered (delete the pragma) or it is structurally unreachable (delete the branch). Leaving an unexplained `continue` in an if/elif chain without justification is exactly the kind of unreasoned control flow that should be refused.

review.summary: The mechanical removal of 3.9 support is largely correct, but the PR ships with the discipline only half-applied. Compatibility scaffolding (`default_raise`, pragma-no-cover comments referencing 3.9, the `kw_only_dataclass` rationale) is left in place even though its precondition no longer holds — this is folklore code. More serious: the stated specification ("Union types will soon not be supported through Ruff") is contradicted by the simultaneous suppression of UP007/UP035/UP045 with a TODO. Either the postcondition holds or it does not; one cannot ship both. Tested-not-proved: CI passing does not constitute a proof that the cleanup is complete.
